Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: natural-history topic cover for an ecology education website, topic 08: bird distribution and abundance across habitats.
Create one new detailed botanical and natural-history illustration, landscape 3:2 composition, approximately 1536 by 1024. Genuine transparent background.

Scene: a single connected broad patch of habitat containing a small wetland inlet at the front-left, rough meadow and grassland across the middle, and a leafy woodland edge at the back-right. Daylight, soft and calm. Several small, naturally proportioned birds occur at different depths: a little wading bird near the water, two ground-foraging birds in the meadow, and two or three birds perched on natural branches. Each bird should belong visually to its place in the habitat. Environment and birds are the focus; no person is needed. The scene suggests that birds occur at different places and numbers across a habitat mosaic, without asserting any measured distribution or population change.

Style and medium: a finely observed natural-history plate painted with layered watercolor and opaque gouache, realistic plants and bird anatomy, tiny individually painted grasses, reeds, leaves, weathered branches and stones. The visual finish should resemble a richly detailed traditional botanical habitat illustration: muted moss greens, olive and umber foliage, warm earth, grey-blue shallow water, restrained natural variation and small subdued bird plumage accents. It is painterly, not a photograph or a cartoon.

Composition: isolated, contiguous landscape patch in natural shallow perspective, wide and balanced, with a low irregular organic perimeter. Ground and vegetation form a connected scene; the edges end in fine leaves, reeds and soft dry-brush watercolor traces that dissolve directly into transparency. Leave transparent space around the entire outside of the scene. There must be no rectangular sky, no opaque background paper, no frame, no cutaway soil walls, and no geometric block or plinth. This is an organic cutout landscape, not an isometric 3D diorama or a rectangular poster.

No text, letters, numbers, labels, legend, arrows, migration paths, tracking lines, charts, diagrams, borders, UI, watermark, floating icons or before-and-after imagery. Do not depict tracking individual birds or a measured decline. The artwork is a conceptual ecological scene, not a field record or scientific result.
